_note: Plain-language definition of every metric in the summary strip (spec 7B.5 and 7A.10). Shown as tooltips.

metrics.label: Airtime
metrics.help: Time each technology is on the air, split into transmit and receive, as a share of the simulation window. Only blocks that really went out are counted; denied blocks are not.

metrics.label: Overlap airtime
metrics.help: How long Bluetooth and Wi-Fi blocks overlapped in time at their planned positions, and how much of that also overlapped in frequency (counting the guard around the Wi-Fi channel).

metrics.label: Conflicts
metrics.help: Number of overlaps that could interact, by severity (hard, degraded, warning, tolerated) and by direction (transmit or receive on each side).

metrics.label: Blocks lost
metrics.help: Blocks that were denied and could not be retried, so their data never went out.

metrics.label: Blocks delayed
metrics.help: Blocks that arbitration moved later because another block won the air first.

metrics.label: Blocks retried
metrics.help: Blocks that were denied and sent again as a new block, up to the retry limit.

metrics.label: Blocks tolerated
metrics.help: Blocks that overlapped another block but did no harm, for example because isolation was high enough.

metrics.label: Not delivered by window end
metrics.help: The strict count: the share of the requested payload that had not been delivered when the window ended, including packets still waiting in a buffer. It is never lower than the throughput impact, which allows a buffered stream to hold a few packets without penalty.

metrics.label: Throughput impact
metrics.help: Share of the requested payload that did not get through: lost, corrupted, or still waiting beyond what the buffer allows (its critical threshold) at the end of the window. Payload counts only blocks that were granted or tolerated and not marked corrupted.

metrics.label: Queued at end
metrics.help: Packets that were delayed and had not been sent when the window ended. A buffered stream may hold packets up to its critical threshold without that counting as an impact.

metrics.label: Added latency
metrics.help: Average and worst extra wait between the planned start of a packet and the start of the block that finally delivered it, including retries. For a buffered stream the i-th delivery is matched with the i-th packet to arrive, as in a queue.

metrics.label: Anchors hit and missed
metrics.help: For tasks with fixed-time activity (voice slots, connection events, beacons): how many events went out as planned and how many were missed.

metrics.label: Longest run of misses
metrics.help: The most anchor events missed one after another. A link drops when too many are missed in a row.

metrics.label: Time before supervision timeout
metrics.help: At the worst point, how much time was left before the link's supervision timer would have expired, given the longest gap between successful events.
